info.name: Clan platform - admin suspension (TEAM-195 to TEAM-200)
info.description:
Tests the admin panel's backend, Phase 1 (TEAM-195 to TEAM-200):

- TEAM-195 migrations: admins, account status, audit log tables (every request below needs them)
- TEAM-196 admin login, admin token type, createadmin tool
- TEAM-197 list developers, developer detail, audit log
- TEAM-198 suspend / resume a developer or a game (+ audit row, idempotent, note stays internal)
- TEAM-199 suspended games: no player tokens, no widget config
- TEAM-200 suspended developers: dashboard read-only, /developers/me shows status

BEFORE YOU RUN
1. Start the stack with migrations 000001-000009 applied: `docker compose up --build` (or `docker compose run --rm platform-migrate` and `go run ./services/platform/cmd`).
2. Create an admin (there is no register endpoint):
   export PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL=postgres://platform_user:<password>@localhost:5432/clan
   printf '%s\n' 'a long password' | go run ./tools/createadmin -email ops@example.com -name "Ops One"
3. Set the collection variables baseUrl (default http://localhost:8081), adminEmail and adminPassword to match.

RUN the whole collection in order (Runner). It makes its own developers and games from a fresh run id, so it can be re-run. It ends with everything resumed.

NOT COVERED: a DISABLED admin cannot log in (needs SQL, see folder 1), and Social / Realtime reacting to a suspension (Phase 3, not built).

item.description: Creates its own developers and games with a fresh run id, so the collection can be re-run. Needs migrations 000001-000009.

item.name: 1. TEAM-195 / TEAM-196: admin login and the admin token type

request.description: A developer account is not an admin account, even with a valid password.
Needs an admin created with: printf '%s\n' '<password>' | go run ./tools/createadmin -email <email> -name "Ops One". Set adminEmail and adminPassword in the collection variables.

exec: pm.test("token and expiresIn", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.token).to.be.a('string').and.not.empty; pm.expect(b.expiresIn).to.be.a('number').and.above(0); });

pm.test("token is an admin token (typ admin)", () => { const p = JSON.parse(atob(pm.response.json().token.split('.')[1].replace(/-/g,'+').replace(/_/g,'/'))); pm.expect(p.typ).to.eql('admin'); pm.expect(p.exp - p.iat).to.eql(pm.response.json().expiresIn); });

pm.test("the admin, without any secret", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.email).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('adminEmail').toLowerCase()); pm.expect(b).to.have.keys('id','email','name','createdAt'); });

item.name: 1.9 Admin me with a DEVELOPER token -> 401
1.10 Admin me with a PLAYER token -> 401
1.11 Developer me with an ADMIN token -> 401

request.description: The token types are not interchangeable in either direction.

item.description:
Proves the admin tables exist (migrations 000007-000009), login works, and an admin token, a developer token and a player token are not interchangeable.

Not covered here because it needs the database: a DISABLED admin cannot log in and its old token stops working at once. Try it by hand: `update admins set disabled_at = now() where email = '<adminEmail>';` then run 1.5 (401 invalid_credentials) and 1.6 with the old token (401); undo with `update admins set disabled_at = null ...;`.

item.name: 2. TEAM-197: list developers, developer detail, audit log (before any suspension)

exec: pm.test("both test developers, newest first", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.developers).to.have.lengthOf(2); pm.expect(b.developers[0].id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('devIdB')); pm.expect(b.developers[1].id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('devId')); pm.expect(b.nextCursor).to.eql(null); });

pm.test("row fields", () => { const d = pm.response.json().developers[1]; pm.expect(d).to.have.keys('id','email','name','status','gameCount','createdAt'); pm.expect(d.status).to.eql('active'); pm.expect(d.gameCount).to.eql(2); pm.expect(pm.response.json().developers[0].gameCount).to.eql(0); });

item.name: 2.2 List, limit=1 -> first page with a cursor

exec: pm.test("one row and a cursor", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.developers).to.have.lengthOf(1); pm.expect(b.developers[0].id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('devIdB')); pm.expect(b.nextCursor).to.be.a('string').and.not.empty; });

item.name: 2.3 List, limit=1 and the cursor -> last page

exec: pm.test("the other developer, and no further cursor", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.developers).to.have.lengthOf(1); pm.expect(b.developers[0].id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('devId')); pm.expect(b.nextCursor).to.eql(null); });

item.name: 2.7 List, % in the search is plain text

exec: pm.test("developer fields", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('devId')); pm.expect(b.email).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('emailA')); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('active'); pm.expect(b.statusReason).to.eql(null); pm.expect(b.statusChangedAt).to.eql(null); });

pm.test("both games with status and reason", () => { const g = pm.response.json().games; pm.expect(g).to.have.lengthOf(2); g.forEach(x => { pm.expect(x).to.have.keys('id','name','description','status','statusReason','statusChangedAt','createdAt'); pm.expect(x.status).to.eql('active'); pm.expect(x.statusReason).to.eql(null); }); });
pm.test("no secrets", () => { const txt = pm.response.text(); pm.expect(txt).to.not.include('password'); pm.expect(txt).to.not.include('$2a$'); });

item.name: 2.16 Audit log of the developer -> empty so far

exec: pm.test("no entries, no cursor", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.entries).to.eql([]); pm.expect(b.nextCursor).to.eql(null); });

item.name: 3. TEAM-198 + TEAM-199: suspend and resume ONE game
3.1 Suspend game A without a reason -> 400
3.2 Suspend game A with an unknown reason -> 400
3.8 Refused calls changed nothing: both games still active

exec: pm.test("suspended with the reason and a time", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('gameIdA')); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('suspended'); pm.expect(b.statusReason).to.eql('abuse'); pm.expect(b.statusChangedAt).to.be.a('string'); });
pm.test("the note is not returned", () => { const txt = pm.response.text(); pm.expect(txt).to.not.include('SECRET-NOTE'); pm.expect(txt).to.not.have.string('"note"'); });

pm.test("nothing changed: same reason, same time", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.statusReason).to.eql('abuse'); pm.expect(b.statusChangedAt).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('gameChangedAt')); });

item.name: 3.11 players/auth, old key of game A -> 403 game_suspended

exec: pm.test("game_suspended and no token", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.error.code).to.eql('game_suspended'); pm.expect(b.token).to.eql(undefined); });

item.name: 3.12 players/auth, invalid body -> still 403 (the game is checked before the body)
3.13 players/auth, wrong key -> 401 (the key is checked first)
3.14 Create a NEW key for the suspended game (the developer is active)
3.15 players/auth, the NEW key of game A -> 403 too

request.description: Every key of a suspended game is refused, old or new: the check is on the game.

item.name: 3.16 widget-config of game A -> 403 game_suspended, not cacheable

exec: pm.test("no ETag, so nothing to revalidate", () => { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.has('ETag')).to.eql(false); });

item.name: 3.18 Game B is not affected: players/auth -> 200
3.19 Game B is not affected: widget-config -> 200
3.20 The developer is still active (a game switch is not an account switch)
3.21 ...so the developer can still edit game B
3.22 Admin detail shows A suspended, B active

exec: pm.test("statuses", () => { const g = pm.response.json().games; const a = g.find(x => x.id === pm.collectionVariables.get('gameIdA')); const b = g.find(x => x.id === pm.collectionVariables.get('gameIdB')); pm.expect(a.status).to.eql('suspended'); pm.expect(a.statusReason).to.eql('abuse'); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('active'); pm.expect(pm.response.json().status).to.eql('active'); });

pm.test("active again, reason cleared, time updated", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('active'); pm.expect(b.statusReason).to.eql(null); pm.expect(b.statusChangedAt).to.be.a('string').and.not.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('gameChangedAt')); });

item.name: 3.25 After resume: old key works again at once
3.26 After resume: the key made while suspended works too

item.description: Validation of the status endpoint, then the effect on the two public entry points: POST /players/auth (game server) and GET /public/games/{id}/widget-config (players' browser).

item.name: 4. TEAM-198 + TEAM-199 + TEAM-200: suspend and resume the DEVELOPER

pm.test("the developer's games keep their own status (the switch is not copied to them)", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); b.games.forEach(g => pm.expect(g.status).to.eql('active')); });
pm.test("the note is not returned", () => { const txt = pm.response.text(); pm.expect(txt).to.not.include('SECRET-NOTE'); pm.expect(txt).to.not.have.string('"note"'); });

pm.test("active again, reason cleared", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('active'); pm.expect(b.statusReason).to.eql(null); pm.expect(b.statusChangedAt).to.be.a('string').and.not.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('devChangedAt')); });

item.name: 4.33 Writes work again at once: register a game

item.description: One switch turns off every game: game servers get 403 account_suspended, players' browsers get 403 game_suspended. The dashboard stays readable (login, every GET) but every write is refused with 403 account_suspended before the body is read, except revoking an API key. Resuming brings everything back at once.

item.name: 5. TEAM-197 + TEAM-198: the audit log after all of the above
5.1 Audit log of the developer: suspended, then resumed (idempotent calls wrote nothing)

exec: pm.test("exactly two entries, newest first", () => { const e = pm.response.json().entries; pm.expect(e).to.have.lengthOf(2); pm.expect(e[0].action).to.eql('developer.resumed'); pm.expect(e[1].action).to.eql('developer.suspended'); });

pm.test("suspension entry: who, why, internal note", () => { const s = pm.response.json().entries[1]; pm.expect(s.actor).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('adminId')); pm.expect(s.targetType).to.eql('developer'); pm.expect(s.targetId).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('devId')); pm.expect(s.reason).to.eql('non_payment'); pm.expect(s.note).to.include('SECRET-NOTE'); });

pm.test("resume entry records the reason it lifted, and its own note", () => { const r = pm.response.json().entries[0]; pm.expect(r.reason).to.eql('non_payment'); pm.expect(r.note).to.eql('paid in full'); });

item.name: 5.2 Audit log of game A: suspended, then resumed

exec: pm.test("two entries for the game", () => { const e = pm.response.json().entries; pm.expect(e).to.have.lengthOf(2); pm.expect(e[0].action).to.eql('game.resumed'); pm.expect(e[1].action).to.eql('game.suspended'); e.forEach(x => { pm.expect(x.targetType).to.eql('game'); pm.expect(x.targetId).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('gameIdA')); }); });
pm.test("reasons", () => { const e = pm.response.json().entries; pm.expect(e[1].reason).to.eql('abuse'); pm.expect(e[0].reason).to.eql('abuse'); pm.expect(e[1].note).to.include('SECRET-NOTE'); });

pm.test("newest entry and a cursor", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.entries).to.have.lengthOf(1); pm.expect(b.entries[0].action).to.eql('developer.resumed'); pm.expect(b.nextCursor).to.be.a('string'); });

pm.test("older entry and no further cursor", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.entries).to.have.lengthOf(1); pm.expect(b.entries[0].action).to.eql('developer.suspended'); pm.expect(b.nextCursor).to.eql(null); });

item.name: 5.5 Audit log of an unrelated target is empty
5.6 Unfiltered audit log is newest first and has at least our four entries

exec: pm.test("at least 4 entries, createdAt never increasing", () => { const e = pm.response.json().entries; pm.expect(e.length).to.be.at.least(4); for (let i = 1; i < e.length; i++) pm.expect(Date.parse(e[i-1].createdAt)).to.be.at.least(Date.parse(e[i].createdAt)); });

item.name: 5.7 Developer detail in the admin panel is back to active

exec: pm.test("active, reason cleared, time kept", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('active'); pm.expect(b.statusReason).to.eql(null); pm.expect(b.statusChangedAt).to.be.a('string'); });
pm.test("the games are all active", () => { pm.response.json().games.forEach(g => pm.expect(g.status).to.eql('active')); });

item.description: Only real changes are in the log: the repeated (idempotent) suspend and resume calls above wrote nothing.
